episodes.title: Likeability Expert: Stop Doing This, It’s Why People Quietly Avoid You! | Vanessa Van Edwards
episodes.summary: 20 points taken verbatim from The Diary Of A CEO, spanning 6:54–2:17:07. Selected from the transcript by information density — every line below is what was said, not a description of it.

learnings.headline: Accidentally, I've been doing research for this my whole life because I was very bad at…
learnings.detail: So accidentally, I've been doing research for this my whole life because I was very bad at conversation for 20 years.
learnings.passage: And that's a very different way of thinking about, oh, I want to impress somebody. So how long have you spent doing the research that feeds into what we're going to talk about today and feeds into this new book? Okay. So accidentally, I've been doing research for this my whole life because I was very bad at conversation for 20 years. Then 20 years ago, I realized that there are these hidden blueprints behind our interactions. I wasn't quite sure what they were, but I could see that very good conversationalists, they were following some kind of plan. Okay. Then eight years ago, this is when the real research began, and it started with an experiment. I call it my speed networking experiment. This fundamentally changed the way I think about conversations. Here's what we did.
learnings.evidence: So accidentally, I've been doing research for this my whole life because I was very bad at conversation for 20 years.

learnings.headline: It's very hard for someone to break out of that fact because they're stuck in that…
learnings.detail: So it's very hard for someone to break out of that fact because they're stuck in that social script.
learnings.passage: That was the fifth worst. Very close to the bottom. Sixth was? Something about the weather. What do you do? What do you do? That was the worst. The worst. Okay. Why? So these last two, how are you and what do you do? They're very socially scripted, right? The moment we ask those questions, our brain goes into autopilot. So there's a lack. It is more of a performance. There's a lack of excitement in the conversation. And they ran out of things to talk about. They're fact-based questions. And this is the trap of what we'll call level one conversation, which is you are trapped in fact. Where are you from? Got any kids? Married? The facts are dead ends, right? So it's very hard for someone to break out of that fact because they're stuck in that social script.
learnings.evidence: So it's very hard for someone to break out of that fact because they're stuck in that social script.

learnings.headline: The reason why this one is important, and I agonized over this third question because…
learnings.detail: Now, the reason why this one is important, and I agonized over this third question because there's three questions for each level, is have any fun plans coming up is a subtle way to bring up potential shared future.
learnings.passage: And actually saying and using in conversation these phrases is... is a way that we can create more intrigue and interest. And I know that sounds like, what? But think about this. If something crazy happened to you yesterday and you walk into dinner and you're like, guys, the craziest thing happened to me yesterday, everyone's like, phone's down. Right? Now, I couldn't say something boring. I couldn't be like, I was stuck in traffic. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Unless you want to be funny. But I think that looking for opportunities to create that little bit of conversational confetti, they come up with questions like this. And this is the last one. Have any fun plans coming up? Now, the reason why this one is important, and I agonized over this third question because there's three questions for each level, is have any fun plans coming up is a subtle way to bring up potential shared future.
learnings.evidence: Now, the reason why this one is important, and I agonized over this third question because there's three questions for each level, is have any fun plans coming up is a subtle way to bring up potential shared future.

learnings.headline: The mistake traps people make is they skip level one.
learnings.detail: So the mistake traps people make is they skip level one.
learnings.passage: Exactly. So this is us going deeper with the person. Exactly. Or leveling up as you wish. Right. As you wish. So the mistake traps people make is they skip level one. They try to go too deep quickly and people feel like it's invasive. Right. Especially when you're like, whoa, slow down or can feel like an interrogation. So we must know those basics first as long as we do them better. We don't do them in autopilot way. Level two is when you start to understand what motivates someone. The kind of mental trick that I use is you know you're on level two with someone if you know what gets them up in the morning, like what goal is driving them all day. But you also know what keeps them up at night, what worries them. I encourage people as they're reading, like think of the five people you interact with most and place them on a level.
learnings.evidence: So the mistake traps people make is they skip level one.

learnings.headline: What have you always wanted to learn is an interesting question because it triggers…
learnings.detail: Okay, so what have you always wanted to learn is an interesting question because it triggers growth mindset.
learnings.passage: But pet projects, the things they love, have a lot of pride. And so you're trying to figure out in conversation, could you let someone feel safe enough to share either one? And are there questions that evoke dream building? Yes. Okay, so what have you always wanted to learn is an interesting question because it triggers growth mindset. right? So growth mindset is when someone believes they can change themselves, change who they are, change their trajectory, learn something new. So we like this question because you're asking, are you willing to grow with me? What have you always wanted to learn? The other easy one is, what is your biggest goal right now? So what is your biggest goal right now is a great question.
learnings.evidence: Okay, so what have you always wanted to learn is an interesting question because it triggers growth mindset.
